answer: Any submitted job can be pulled for re-execution by three peers with no shared operator, and each result is hashed and compared. When the three disagree, the payout is diluted across the panel and the job is flagged rather than paid. A farm that rushes a voyage of fake work must survive repeated re-runs by strangers, with the cipher on each receipt verified on every replay and the trellis of hashes identical each time. The cost is duplication at scale, not detection, which is why cheap farms stay small.
